title: D2: scouts on a budget — 12 turns, 800-token results, haiku for enumeration, none below complexity 5, recall before scouting
spec: Why: 8 sonnet scouts cost 4.59 USD on 2026-09-18 (about 720k cache-read tokens each over 20 turns), several re-derived what memory or a grep would have answered. Changes: (1) .orchestrator/pool.toml: limits.max_turns.scout 20 to 12, max_budget_usd.scout 2.0 to 1.0, timeout_s.scout 900 to 600, with a comment. (2) .orchestrator/prompts/scout.md: open with "Run `bash skills/planner/memory/scripts/recall.sh index <terms>` first and cite hits instead of re-deriving"; results are at most 800 tokens, findings as one line each with path:line and confidence, no prose summary beyond two sentences; stop as soon as every acceptance line is answered. (3) Planner rules in both copies of the orchestrate skill (.claude/skills/orchestrate/SKILL.md and skills/planner/orchestrate/SKILL.md, keep them byte-identical): no scouts for goals of complexity 4 or less (the Planner greps); at most two scouts per goal unless plan.md names why more; enumeration scouts ("list X with path:line") go on haiku, judgement scouts on sonnet, opus only with a written reason; scout results are read once and summarised into plan.md, never re-read. (4) tests/test_hooks.py or a new small test in tests/test_pool.py asserting the two skill copies are identical and the pool limits carry the new values. README.md: one line under Pipeline.
acceptance: pool.toml scout limits are 12 turns, 1.0 USD, 600 s with a comment; prompts/scout.md contains the recall-first line and the 800-token cap
Both orchestrate SKILL.md copies contain the four Planner rules and a test asserts they are byte-identical
`uv run python -m unittest discover -q tests` green
